report_name: Emperador Ransomware Group Claims Attack on Italian Notary Firm

threat_actors.name: Emperador
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that conducted a double-extortion attack against an Italian notary firm, claiming to have stolen thousands of sensitive documents.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
attack_patterns.description: The Emperador group is alleged to have moved laterally through the victim's network to identify and steal thousands of sensitive documents before encryption.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The Emperador group deployed ransomware to encrypt files across the network of an Italian notary firm as part of a double-extortion attack.

attack_patterns.name: Financial Theft
attack_patterns.description: The Emperador group demanded a ransom payment from the victim in exchange for a decryption key and a promise not to leak the stolen data.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: A common ransomware precursor technique mentioned for hunting is the deletion of volume shadow copies using 'vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet' to prevent system restore.

malware.name: Emperador Ransomware
malware.description: Ransomware used by the Emperador group to encrypt files and facilitate a double-extortion attack against an Italian notary firm.

identities.name: Studio Notarile Associato Salvatore Costantino E Anna Favarato
identities.description: An Italian notary firm targeted by the Emperador ransomware group, from which thousands of sensitive legal, financial, and personal identification documents were allegedly stolen.

indicators.name: Ransomware Volume Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: Ransomware Volume Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 2b9a1c3d-f4e5-4b6c-8d7e-9f0a1b2c3d4e
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common precursor to ransomware encryption.
references:
  - https://www.dexpose.io/intel-feeds/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-21
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative activity, though rare for deleting all shadows.
level: high
indicators.description: Detects command line execution of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware tactic to inhibit system recovery.

indicators.name: Potential Ransomware Data Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Ransomware Data Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
id: 8e7f6d5c-4b3a-4c2d-1b0a-9f8e7d6c5b4a
status: experimental
description: Detects network connections to known cloud storage providers that can be used for data exfiltration during a ransomware attack.
references:
  - https://www.dexpose.io/intel-feeds/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-21
tags:
  - attack.t1567.002
  - attack.exfiltration
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    cs-host|contains:
      - 'mega.io'
      - 'pcloud.com'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate use of these cloud storage services. Volume thresholds are needed for higher fidelity.
level: medium
indicators.description: Detects large, sustained data uploads to known cloud storage providers like Mega.io or pCloud, which can indicate the data exfiltration phase of a double-extortion ransomware attack.

indicators.name: Ransomware File Extension Renaming
indicators.pattern:
title: Ransomware File Extension Renaming
id: 5a4b3c2d-1e0f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4d3c2b1a
status: experimental
description: Detects file rename events where a file extension associated with ransomware is added.
references:
  - https://www.dexpose.io/intel-feeds/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-21
tags:
  - attack.t1486
  - attack.impact
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.emperador'
      - '.locked'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Benign files that happen to use a similar extension.
level: high
indicators.description: Detects files being renamed with a new, uniform extension (e.g., .emperador, .locked), which is a strong indicator of an active ransomware encryption process.
